message: Never merge while checks are pending; run `gh pr checks <n> --watch` first.
spawnSync in a vitest test file risks the silent multi-hour CI hang class; use async spawn with a SIGKILL deadline instead.

Standing Order 7: no stash save/push in a shared checkout - it sweeps sibling agents' uncommitted work (2026-08-19/20, 23 files lost). Work in a git worktree. Recovery ops (pop/apply/drop/list/show) are allowed.
Force-push is ASK-FIRST (operator policy). NEVER on a stacked-PR branch (false-MERGED class) - use gh stack sync / gh stack push. Personal single branch after a rebase: confirm.
Force-with-lease push — confirm this is intended before overwriting remote history.
Destructive git operation — on the operator ASK-FIRST list.

Before dispatching: PATH-prepend in command verifications, no absolute cd (cwd is the task worktree), no | tail on gates, intent verifications for worktree files, base-sha stamp + drift check, and know the STOP conditions.
Open-ended gh polling loop with sleep < 60s risks the 5,000/hr API budget; use sleep >= 60 or `gh run watch` / `gh pr checks --watch`.

Piping a test run into tail/grep/head makes the pipeline's exit status the filter's, not the tests'. Gate on the test command's own exit code (run it once to a log, then read the log); if you must match output, strip ANSI first - unittest/cargo print colored OK/FAILED.
source: gate-verdict priors: never | tail on gates

message: Flat hex-events policies (top-level trigger/action) are silently skipped by the daemon; use the rules: list format and validate with `cd ~/.hex-events && venv/bin/python hex_events_cli.py validate`.
A full memory reindex can resurrect stale facts from raw transcripts — confirm this is intended.

hex-events is the only automation system (CLAUDE.md). Built-in scheduling (CronCreate / ScheduleWakeup) is for a deliberate operator /loop only - approve if you asked for it; otherwise write a hex-events policy.
Exa is the default for web research, not the built-in WebSearch tool — confirm this is intentional.

Unquoted heredoc delimiter with a backtick in the body: the shell executes the backtick text as a command substitution (twice on 2026-09-06 a note was lost this way). Quote the delimiter (<<'EOF') or pass the text via a variable/file, then verify the artifact was written.
